issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for class SealSaloon: the problem statement UML and text declare a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts the saloon name (see problem_statement.md), but both the provided template usage (Main.java) and the reference solution implement and call a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This inconsistency will confuse students about which constructor to implement and how to instantiate SealSaloon.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred if the saloon name is not needed): update the problem statement/UML to specify a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() and remove the text requiring a String parameter. Option B (if the name should be stored): update the template and solution to provide a constructor public SealSaloon(String name), store the name in a field (and add a getter), and update Main and any examples/tests to call new SealSaloon("SomeName"). Ensure the UML, problem text, template Main, and solution implementation all match the chosen constructor signature.
